prompts.truck:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a high-resolution polished 360-degree asset turnaround concept sheet for HAVENLINE, a premium stylized winter-survival mobile game. Landscape 3:2 sheet on subtle deep navy presentation background, exceptionally clear chunky rounded sculpted 3D game art, colorful warm wood and blue-orange industrial equipment, soft snow caps, attractive tactile PBR-like illustrated materials, clean friendly heroic proportions, not photorealism and not gritty military.

SUBJECT: One consistent player-drivable heavy SNOW TRUCK. Squat rounded cobalt-blue single cabin with large icy cyan windows, orange fenders and armor trims, navy utility cargo bed, dark gray chassis, four massive thick snow tires (two on each side), silver hubs, warm small headlamps, compact amber roof beacon, modest snow on upper ledges. Behind cabin a broad open cargo bin with a SMALL representative mixed stack of logs, ore, metal ingots and food crates, no implication of a finite inventory limit. Truck is heavy, capable and exciting, recognizable at mobile gameplay scale.

CRITICAL BOTTOM BLADES: A rugged orange low front-mounted cutting deck projects ahead of the front wheels. TWO large side-by-side steel rotary circular cutting discs on short VERTICAL spindle axes. Both blade discs lie FLAT HORIZONTAL, PARALLEL TO THE SNOW/GROUND, near ground level. Their forward toothed silver cutting rims are clearly visible extending beyond the protective orange deck. Thick rugged teeth can fell trees, smash mining rocks and strike game enemies. Blades are not vertical saw wheels, not a snowplow scoop, not a snowblower or lawnmower. Short heavy-duty armored pivots support the cutting deck from the chassis. Clear safe mechanical separation from tires, aligned across every angle.

LAYOUT: Six comfortably separated panels with no overlap or cropping. Top row three true cardinal views: FRONT, RIGHT, REAR. Bottom row: LEFT cardinal side view, large FRONT THREE-QUARTER beauty view with horizontal blades clearly legible, and TOP DETAIL of the bottom blade assembly showing the two discs lying in one horizontal plane and attachment to the truck. Every view must show the EXACT SAME truck wheel count, chassis, cabin, cargo, attachments and proportions. Opposite sides truly differ by viewing side; rear is rear, not duplicated front. Ground-contact shadows; full tires and blades within frame.

Typography minimal and premium: title exactly "HAVENLINE | SNOW TRUCK". Small clean panel labels exactly "FRONT", "RIGHT", "REAR", "LEFT", "THREE-QUARTER", "HORIZONTAL BLADE DETAIL". No stats, prices, extra logos, human figures, weapons on roof, guns, arrows or callout leader lines. Studio asset presentation, no scene or map. This is authored concept art for a fictional game vehicle, no engineering schematic.
prompts.garage_r1:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a polished high-resolution 360-degree turnaround sheet of ONE consistently designed snow-truck GARAGE for HAVENLINE, stylized premium winter-survival mobile game. Landscape 3:2 sheet, six well-spaced panels on deep navy presentation background, clean chunky rounded sculpted 3D game art, warm orange timber beams, cobalt blue roof and roll-up door, broad dark steel straps and silver bolts, rounded gray stone foundation, soft white snow roof caps, warm interior lights. Match a charming strong stylized snow camp, NOT photorealistic, NOT gritty, not flimsy.

GARAGE GEOMETRY must be coherent in every view: One rectangular single-bay garage sits INSIDE a camp immediately against its perimeter fence. Its FRONT external overhead roll-up garage door REPLACES one section of the camp fence, not a building set behind an intact fence. Substantial orange-brown pointed log palisade fence wings connect directly to the front LEFT and RIGHT corner posts and continue laterally in a single boundary line. Snow caps on log tips, clear thick vertical stakes and rope rails. The garage building extends backward INTO CAMP. Rear camp-side facade has a WIDE PERMANENTLY OPEN timber-framed vehicle arch (a different view of the same THROUGH BAY); large enough for full truck and side pedestrian access, no second exterior fence. Both long side walls are solid. Simple small square workshop window on one side, a low orange-trimmed resource output hatch on the other. Snow blue pitched roof, orange eaves and substantial structural pillars. Tiny gear-and-truck badge above exterior door, no numbers or fictitious signage.

WIDTH/FIT: The bay is generously sized for one blue-orange four-wheel heavy truck with LOW horizontal twin-saw front cutting deck, and permits genuine circulation along sides. Front roll-up opening at least 1.5 times full blade-deck width and tall enough for beacon. Bay length encloses entire truck including blades; no saws sticking into closing door. Interior has a discrete dark charcoal docking platform with a thin warm amber inset perimeter and small resource/crate icon near wall. All built floor stays INSIDE the camp-side garage footprint; OUTSIDE the exterior fence threshold is natural snow, not a painted road or paved path.

SHEET COMPOSITION, six panels:
Top row FRONT (door closed, fence wings visible), RIGHT (true right side, front to image right), REAR (camp-facing OPEN ARCH, look through bay to blue closed exterior door), bottom row LEFT (true opposite side, front to image left), OPEN GARAGE (large elevated FRONT three-quarter, exterior door rolled fully up, truck parked fully inside bay facing outward, full low horizontal blades clearly inside threshold; fence wings attach front corners), CUTAWAY (roof removed high rear/camp-side three-quarter showing the continuous full-depth bay, opposite exterior door, truck parking footprint, access beside truck and side output hatch). Consistent roof, foundation, proportions, door positions and fence connections. Studio sheet; avoid perspective contradictions and repeated same-side panels. Truck stays the same chunky cobalt blue cabin, orange fenders, navy cargo bed, FOUR large gray snow tires, two horizontally flat steel saw discs on orange deck at ground level, mixed logs/ore/ingots/food cargo. Truck must not appear 6-wheel or tracked.

Minimal clean white exact typography: title "HAVENLINE | SNOW TRUCK GARAGE"; panel labels "FRONT", "RIGHT", "REAR / CAMP SIDE", "LEFT", "OPEN GARAGE", "CUTAWAY / DOCKING". No extra text, stats, dimension lines, arrows, humans, additional trucks or price. All views fully in frame, no overlapping panels. Clear authored concept-art presentation, not an engineering schematic.

CRITICAL FIX: CUTAWAY must show ONE truck only, with ONE cabin and FOUR wheels total, in a continuous single garage bay. This panel is viewed from the open REAR/CAMP-SIDE entrance toward the closed blue external garage door at the FAR end. The truck points AWAY from the viewer toward that FAR external door. Therefore its REAR open navy cargo bed and tailgate are closest to the viewer; its one cobalt-blue cabin with amber beacon is farther away, near the far end. Its orange front blade deck with two flat horizontal steel discs is at the FAR FRONT of the truck, behind the cabin from this camera, with clear space before the closed exterior door. Do not put a second front, grille, cabin or blade deck at the near/camp-side end. Keep the bay visibly longer and wider than the whole truck; all of the truck is inside the docking outline and door closure planes. Show side walk clearance. Full roof removed as a cutaway, same orange walls, bolts, foundation and docking pad. Small representative mixed logs/ore/ingot/food cargo in rear bed, not an extra cab.

OPEN GARAGE illustration: retain one truck facing toward viewer/outside, fully inside threshold. Make the front truck match the companion design: ONE squat rounded cobalt blue cabin, orange fenders, dark navy bed, FOUR heavy tires, two vertical dark metal support arms running from high front bumper down to its orange blade deck; two obvious horizontal silver saw discs at very bottom. Distinct silver/gray vertical front grille between two warm yellow headlights. Maintain an ample garage opening around truck and blade deck, no crossing the doorway threshold.

No additional vehicles, no new panels, no extra writing. This is a targeted correction to prevent duplicate vehicle geometry and maintain front/rear orientation.
